intent: Hold the iteration-3 geometry exactly: five sensors at y = 0.06 m with x from -0.024 to +0.024 m, 12 mm footprints, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.14 by 0.16 m body, and 0.6 kg mass. The mass change is kept because it gave the best score so far and the s-bend completion held at 0.6. I expect the same or better oval and s-bend results, with the slalom still limited by late reaction. The aim is to isolate controller changes. If slalom max_error stays at or above 0.06 m with line losses at or below 2 per run, my next geometry change is the forward offset, y = 0.07 m, with the spread unchanged. I am considering, but not committing to, a wider spread (±0.032 m) only if slalom line losses rise above 2 per run.
learning: Hypotheses for this race: (1) with the geometry held, slalom max_error stays near 0.06 m, which would show the remaining limit is look-ahead rather than mass or sensing; (2) the s-bend completion stays at or above 0.5; (3) line_loss_events stay at or below 2 per run on all tracks. If (1) holds and (3) holds, the next geometry test is y = 0.07 m. If (3) fails on the slalom, the spread is the next lever. Iteration 3 gave a useful signal: the mass change helped the s-bend (completion 0.3 to 0.6) without hurting the oval, so yaw inertia is a real lever even though oscillation did not fall as predicted.
rationale:
Iteration 3 (mass 0.6 kg, otherwise unchanged) is the best race so far at 575.8, up from 501.2. The oval still completes 20 of 20 and its oscillation fell to 0.21 from 0.21 (no change worth acting on). The s-bend completes 12 of 20 (up from 6), and its max_error is 0.0447 m. The slalom still fails 0 of 20, with progress 0.1975 and max_error 0.0645 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit, and line losses at 1.0 per run.

I checked the Integrator's trigger rules against this race. (a) Widen the spread to ±0.032 m only if slalom line losses exceed about 2 per run with progress below 0.2. Line losses are 1.0, so this does not fire. (b) Revert toward 0.8 kg only if s-bend completion falls below 0.3. It is 0.6, so this does not fire. (c) Keep 0.6 kg if oval oscillation falls below about 0.15 and slalom max_error reaches 0.06 m or less. Neither condition is met, but the mass change still improved the score and the s-bend, and the Integrator's controller was also changed in this iteration, so I read the result as the best available evidence for 0.6 kg rather than a failure of it. The body is still not a lever: its width sets the off-track limit at the 0.06 m floor.

I am keeping the geometry unchanged. The main unresolved lever is the slalom's late reaction (max_error just above the limit with few line losses). The look-ahead change from y = 0.04 to 0.06 m helped in iteration 1, so a further forward move to y = 0.07 m is the next candidate, but changing it now would confound the controller changes the Integrator is making. I will hold the 0.6 kg geometry this iteration, so that the controller is the only changing variable, and test y = 0.07 m next if slalom max_error stays at or above 0.06 m.
